data.body:
## Root cause proven; fix pushed as Gerrit change 2337

**Mechanism (confirmed, not inferred).** Sign and verify resolve the op-cert key from two
different places:

- SIGN: `ensure_opcert_key` (`_opcert_signing.py:155-206`) takes the context-local startup
  binding first. `compose_startup_opcert_binding` (`mcp_server.py:717-746`) composes it from
  `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, and `run_mcp` binds it around the whole
  serving loop (`_mcp_health.py:325-329`), so every tool call — sign AND verify — runs inside it.
- VERIFY: `_opcert_own_public_key` (`:238-258`) consulted neither the binding nor
  `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`; it read `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub` and self-healed only from
  `<tracker>/.opcert-key`.

Live read-only probe of the deployed container (`rebar-mcp-afe01efaa8b2-8092`,
i-00880b2c7f13527c5) on 2026-08-28:

```
REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=UNSET      REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=SET
REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=SET          REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY=UNSET
/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets/: .env-id only — no .opcert-key, no .opcert-key.pub
/run/secrets/: opcert-ed25519-key (0600, private half only)
```

The tracker has NO `.opcert-key` even though the server signs successfully. That is the proof
the binding is observed on the sign path: unbound and override-less, the first
`ensure_opcert_key(create_if_missing=True)` would have generated one there.

**Gerrit change 2328 (`seaborne-wisdomless-songbird`) does not fix this.** Its premise — "the
ContextVar binding is not observed on every tool-call path, so no step yields a key" — is
refuted by the two facts above. `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` is read only by the SIGN-side
`ensure_opcert_key`, which the bound server never falls through to, and the failing VERIFY-side
reader never consults it. Setting it is a no-op for this failure: neither necessary (signing
already works) nor sufficient (verification still returns `foreign_key`). A regression test
here (`test_key_path_override_cert_certifies_in_the_same_environment`) reproduces exactly
2328's config and is RED without the code fix. Recommend abandoning 2328.

**Fix (change 2337).** Verification resolves the public half from the same ordered chain the
signing side resolves the private half (binding → `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` → tracker genesis),
deriving the public line in-process with `ssh-keygen -y` and taking every key the environment
holds as the trust root. `_derive_opcert_pub` now returns the derived text as well as caching
it, because a bind-mounted secret's directory is read-only and the cache can never be written
there. No deploy change, no new secret.

**Mutation-checked.** With the fix reverted, 3 of the 4 tests fail with the exact production
reason ("this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature"); with
it, all 4 pass. The 4th (tracker genesis) passes both ways and is the regression oracle.

Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`,
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0 increased=0) all pass; 1017 opcert/signing/attest
tests pass.

**Scope.** AC1-AC4 of the revised plan are addressed. AC5 (warn at mint when the environment
cannot verify its own signature) and AC6 (deploy health check) remain open follow-ups; with
this fix the key-path divergence that produced the silent uncertifiable cert is no longer
reachable, but neither guard exists yet. AC1's on-box demonstration needs 2337 deployed.

Related but distinct: `gold-distinct-lacewing` (eca3) is the `.env-id` re-identification bug
(principal mismatch); this one is the absent public key. Different verdict, different mechanism.
